title: Trump: Former Trump executive releases book detailing racism & stupidity
description_short: Trump: Former Trump executive releases book detailing racism & stupidity
description_medium: John R. O'Donnell, a former Trump Plaza Hotel and Casino president, published Trumped! in 1991. The linked archive reproduces selected passages from a July 14 New York Times review discussing his claims about Trump's remarks and business conduct. The excerpts attribute those claims to O'Donnell; the archive gives no exact book release date, complete review or underlying pages to verify each passage.
description_long: John R. O'Donnell, a former president of Trump Plaza Hotel and Casino, published Trumped! The Inside Story of the Real Donald Trump in 1991. The linked archive says the book reached stores around the time of a May 1, 1991 entry and reproduces selected excerpts from a New York Times review published July 14. The review summarized O'Donnell's account of racist remarks about Black accountants and his claims about Trump's response to a 1989 helicopter crash and casino spending. Those allegations are attributed to O'Donnell and summarized by the reviewer; the excerpts do not independently verify them. The archive does not supply a precise publication-day record, the full review or the underlying book pages needed to check the passages in context. The available material supports describing the book and the review, while leaving the exact release chronology and full quotations unconfirmed.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Former Trump executive releases book detailing racism & stupidity
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Former Trump executive releases book detailing racism & stupidity

notes: Source reading: The archive identifies O'Donnell's 1991 book and reproduces selected passages from a July 14, 1991 New York Times review. It gives no exact release date and not the full review or underlying book text; the allegations remain attributed to O'Donnell.

title: Donald Trump taps Vanity Fair to help him launch his comeback
description_short: Donald Trump taps Vanity Fair to help him launch his comeback
description_medium: In December 1993, Donald Trump asked Vanity Fair to profile him as he sought to rebuild his public image. The magazine assigned Edward Klein to spend several days with Trump that month, and published the feature in March 1994. The account describes a request and editorial access, but does not show that Vanity Fair promised promotion or favorable coverage.
description_long: Donald Trump asked Vanity Fair for a profile in December 1993 as he tried to rebuild his public image after business setbacks. The magazine assigned writer Edward Klein to spend several days with him during the month, and published the resulting feature in March 1994. The linked archive quotes Klein describing Trump's belief that the press could “build you back up” after cutting you down, and places the request alongside Trump's financial difficulties and planned public offering. The account documents a profile Trump sought and the access Klein received while reporting it. It does not indicate that Vanity Fair entered a promotional agreement or guaranteed favorable coverage. The resulting feature was editorial coverage produced by the magazine; the request and interview access do not establish a business partnership or endorsement.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump taps Vanity Fair to help him launch his comeback
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump taps Vanity Fair to help him launch his comeback

notes: Source reading: The linked archive says Trump requested a feature, Edward Klein spent several days with him in December 1993, and the profile appeared in March 1994. It documents access for an editorial profile, not a promotional arrangement or promise of favorable coverage.

title: Trump: FBI reports on Semion Mogilevich's transnational organized crime operation
description_short: Trump: FBI reports on Semion Mogilevich's transnational organized crime operation
description_medium: A 1996 FBI report described the Semion Mogilevich Organization as a transnational criminal group of about 250 people and summarized alleged operations and business links. It mentioned associates in the Russian government while noting investigative limits. The reproduced assessment does not establish that the government directed the organization or connect Mogilevich to Donald Trump; the timeline's placement alone is not evidence of a relationship.
description_long: An FBI report prepared for law-enforcement use in 1996 described the Semion Mogilevich Organization as a transnational criminal group of about 250 people. It summarized a multinational investigative working group's findings about alleged operations, businesses, finances and contacts in several countries. The report referred to associates in the Russian government but also qualified what investigators could trace. That language does not establish that the Russian government directed the organization or that every alleged connection was proven. The linked page reproduces the assessment but does not supply corroborating records for each government connection. It offers no evidence linking Mogilevich or his organization to Donald Trump. The report can be described as an FBI assessment of alleged organized-crime activity, with its stated limits kept in view; the connection to Trump and broader claims about the intelligence relationship remain unsupported by the cited material.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: FBI reports on Semion Mogilevich's transnational organized crime operation
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: FBI reports on Semion Mogilevich's transnational organized crime operation

notes: Source reading: The reproduced 1996 FBI report describes an approximately 250-member organization and alleged Russian-government associates, with qualifications about investigative limits. title: Trump World Tower opens, uses mafia to sell condos to Russia
description_short: Trump World Tower opens, uses mafia to sell condos to Russia
description_medium: A 2017 Bloomberg investigation reported that buyers from Russia and neighboring countries owned many upper-floor Trump World Tower units. Broker Dolly Lenz estimated she sold about 65 apartments to Russian buyers; the article said regional buyers held roughly a third of units on floors 76–83 by 2004. Bloomberg also described Moscow marketing and German-bank financing, but did not establish that a criminal group brokered the sales.
description_long: Trump World Tower opened in Manhattan in 2001 while the Trump Organization carried substantial debt from its Atlantic City properties. A 2017 Bloomberg investigation reported that wealthy buyers from Russia and neighboring countries purchased apartments in the building. Broker Dolly Lenz estimated she sold about 65 units to Russian buyers, and the article said people or companies with regional ties owned roughly one-third of units on floors 76 through 83 by 2004. Bloomberg also described marketing in Moscow and financing tied to German banks. Some buyers had faced allegations or investigations involving organized crime or money laundering, but those cases concerned individual purchasers; they do not show a criminal group arranged the tower's sales. The report offers estimates and ownership research rather than a complete buyer ledger. It does not establish that the Trump Organization used organized crime to market units or that Trump knew of alleged criminal activity by buyers.

preserved_fields.title: Trump World Tower opens, uses mafia to sell condos to Russia
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump World Tower opens, uses mafia to sell condos to Russia

notes: Source reading: Bloomberg reports Lenz's estimate of about 65 Russian buyers, regional ownership of about a third of upper-floor units by 2004, Moscow marketing and German-bank financing. The linked reporting does not provide a complete buyer ledger or establish criminal-group brokerage; the title's “uses mafia” claim is unsupported by it.

title: Trump: The Apprentice, created by Putin collaborator, premieres on NBC
description_short: Trump: The Apprentice, created by Putin collaborator, premieres on NBC
description_medium: Mark Burnett pursued Destination: Mir, an unrealized reality competition tied to Russia's Mir space station, before The Apprentice premiered on NBC in 2004. A 2001 New York Times Magazine account quoted Burnett saying, “Putin is involved,” about the earlier project. The sources do not show that Putin collaborated on The Apprentice or influenced Trump's selection as host.
description_long: Before The Apprentice premiered on NBC in 2004, producer Mark Burnett pursued a separate reality-TV concept called Destination: Mir. The proposed competition was tied to Russia's Mir space station, and Burnett was negotiating with Russian officials. A 2001 New York Times Magazine account quoted him saying, “Putin is involved,” referring to that project. Destination: Mir did not become The Apprentice and did not proceed after plans for Mir changed. The source establishes that Burnett described Russian involvement in negotiations for the separate proposal. It does not show that Vladimir Putin collaborated with Burnett on The Apprentice, took part in choosing Donald Trump as host or influenced the NBC program's creation. Burnett's work on both concepts connects them through their producer, but does not establish a Putin partnership on the series. The title's broader claim is not supported by the linked account.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: The Apprentice, created by Putin collaborator, premieres on NBC
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: The Apprentice, created by Putin collaborator, premieres on NBC

notes: Source reading: The linked archive reproduces a 2001 New York Times Magazine passage in which Burnett said Putin was involved in negotiations for Destination: Mir. It was a separate, unrealized space-station project; the source does not connect Putin to The Apprentice's creation or casting.

title: Donald Trump announces Trump SoHo, developed by criminals Sater & Arif
description_short: Donald Trump announces Trump SoHo, developed by criminals Sater & Arif
description_medium: Trump SoHo was developed by Bayrock Group and the Sapir Organization, with the Trump Organization supplying its name and management. Bayrock executive Felix Sater pleaded guilty to racketeering in a stock-manipulation case and later cooperated with federal investigators. A Manhattan investigation into buyer allegations closed without charges; the linked reporting does not establish criminal conduct by co-developer Tevfik Arif or the Trump Organization.
description_long: The Trump Organization announced Trump SoHo as a condominium-hotel project developed with Bayrock Group and the Sapir Organization. The New York Times reported that Bayrock executive Felix Sater promoted real-estate projects with Trump and that the Trump Organization supplied the building's name and management. Court records show Sater pleaded guilty in 1998 to racketeering connected to a $40 million stock-manipulation scheme involving organized-crime figures; he later cooperated with federal investigators. The Times described Sater as an unindicted co-conspirator in a later indictment and reported that a Manhattan investigation into Trump SoHo buyers' fraud allegations closed without criminal charges. Trump said he did not know Sater well and was surprised by his past. These records establish Sater's conviction and Bayrock's role, but do not establish a criminal conviction for co-developer Tevfik Arif or criminal conduct by the Trump Organization.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump announces Trump SoHo, developed by criminals Sater & Arif
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump announces Trump SoHo, developed by criminals Sater & Arif

notes: Source reading: The Times reports Bayrock's partnership in Trump SoHo, Sater's 1998 racketeering plea and cooperation, and a Manhattan investigation that closed without charges. Trump said he did not know Sater well. The linked material does not establish a criminal conviction for Arif or criminal conduct by the Trump Organization.

title: Trump: Felix Sater: Mafia, Trump, FBI, CIA, and Money Laundering
description_short: Trump: Felix Sater: Mafia, Trump, FBI, CIA, and Money Laundering
description_medium: Felix Sater worked for Bayrock Group, a partner in Trump SoHo, and promoted real-estate projects with Donald Trump. Court records document Sater's 1998 guilty plea to racketeering in a $40 million stock-manipulation scheme and his later cooperation with U.S. authorities. The reporting documents a business association but does not establish Trump's involvement in Sater's crimes or in the intelligence work Sater later claimed.
description_long: Felix Sater's 1998 guilty plea to racketeering in a $40 million stock-manipulation scheme and his later cooperation with U.S. authorities are documented in court records and contemporaneous reporting. Sater worked for Bayrock Group, which partnered with the Trump Organization on Trump SoHo, and promoted real-estate projects with Donald Trump. The New York Times reported that Trump said he did not know Sater well and was surprised by his criminal past. The article describes Sater's role at Bayrock and the property partnership; it does not show that Trump participated in the stock scheme or in an intelligence operation. Sater later made claims about work with government agencies, but the linked material does not supply records to corroborate those claims. The business association and Sater's criminal case are separate facts, and do not establish that Trump was involved in money laundering, organized crime or intelligence work.

preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Felix Sater: Mafia, Trump, FBI, CIA, and Money Laundering

title: Trump: Michael Caputo moves to Ukraine to aid Putin in political takeover
description_short: Trump: Michael Caputo moves to Ukraine to aid Putin in political takeover
description_medium: Michael Caputo moved to Ukraine in 2007 to consult for the Bloc Lytvyn, led by Volodymyr Lytvyn. The linked archive notes Lytvyn received Russia's Order of Friendship and was photographed with Vladimir Putin, but provides no evidence Putin directed Caputo's work or that the campaign was a political takeover. Caputo's earlier job at Gazprom Media does not establish who commissioned or controlled the Ukrainian campaign.
description_long: Michael Caputo moved to Ukraine in 2007 to consult for the Bloc Lytvyn, a party led by Volodymyr Lytvyn. The linked archive connects Lytvyn to Vladimir Putin by noting that he received Russia's Order of Friendship and was photographed with the Russian president. It does not provide a contract, campaign record or other evidence that Putin directed Caputo's consulting or that the campaign was part of a political takeover. Caputo had previously worked for Gazprom Media in Russia, which documents earlier professional ties to the country but does not show who commissioned or controlled his Ukrainian work. The account identifies the consultant and party, while the alleged Putin direction rests on association rather than evidence of control. The title's claim that Caputo moved to Ukraine to aid a Putin-led takeover is not established by the cited material.

title: Trump: The Tea Party, funded by Koch brothers, aims to take over the Republican party
description_short: Trump: The Tea Party, funded by Koch brothers, aims to take over the Republican party
description_medium: The linked archive describes the Tea Party as a movement organized in part by Americans for Prosperity and allied conservative groups. It alleges Koch funding and an effort to reshape Republican politics, but supplies no complete grant ledger or records showing how much each group received. Its account does not document a specific change in Republican leadership or establish that the movement took control of the party.
description_long: The linked Trump Timeline article describes early Tea Party activity as involving Americans for Prosperity, the State Policy Network, the Sam Adams Alliance and other conservative organizations. It alleges that the Koch brothers funded parts of the movement and that those groups sought to reshape the Republican Party's agenda. The page does not provide a complete grant ledger identifying amounts, recipients and dates, or records showing how each group influenced party leaders. It also does not identify a specific leadership change that would substantiate the title's claim that the movement took over the party. The source supports describing an allegation of coordinated conservative organizing and a stated political aim. It does not establish the scale of Koch funding or demonstrate a takeover of Republican leadership. Financial records and documentation of specific organizational changes would be needed to support those claims.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: The Tea Party, funded by Koch brothers, aims to take over the Republican party
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: The Tea Party, funded by Koch brothers, aims to take over the Republican party

title: Trump: Daily Beast releases fluff piece on Jeffrey Epstein, featuring Wilbur Ross
description_short: Trump: Daily Beast releases fluff piece on Jeffrey Epstein, featuring Wilbur Ross
description_medium: Alexandra Wolfe's 2011 Daily Beast article described Jeffrey Epstein's access to New York social circles after his Florida conviction. It quoted an unnamed socialite blaming a teenage victim who had lied about her age, and reported that Wilbur Ross attended a screening with Epstein. Ross was not quoted. An email forwarding the article is dated April 3, 2011, but the article's exact publication date is unclear.
description_long: Alexandra Wolfe's Daily Beast article “Jeffrey Epstein's Society Friends Close Ranks” described Epstein's continued access to New York social circles after his Florida conviction. It said former Bear Stearns chief James Cayne had endorsed Epstein's science foundation and quoted an unnamed socialite: “I've never condoned paying for sex, but if the young lady lied about her age it's her own fault.” The article also noted that Wilbur Ross and real-estate investor Leon Black socialized with Epstein at a Southampton movie screening two months after Epstein's release from community control. Ross appears as an attendee, not as the speaker of the victim-blaming remark. An email forwarding the article is dated April 3, 2011, though the original publication date is not established. The quotation reflects one social acquaintance's view and should not be attributed to Ross or treated as the publication's own conclusion.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Daily Beast releases fluff piece on Jeffrey Epstein, featuring Wilbur Ross
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Daily Beast releases fluff piece on Jeffrey Epstein, featuring Wilbur Ross

notes: Source reading: The archived Daily Beast text includes the unnamed socialite's quoted blame of a young woman who lied about her age and says Wilbur Ross attended a screening with Epstein but was not quoted. The forwarding email is dated Apr. 3, 2011; the article's exact publication date is not established.
